subject: general
question: Which of the following is a Middle Indian dialect that is closely related to Sanskrit, and is one of the major languages of Buddhist scriptures and literature?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Pali** is an ancient Middle Indian language that is closely related to Sanskrit.
 
• It is the language in which the earliest Buddhist scriptures, known as the Pali Canon or Tipitaka, were composed.
 
• Pali is considered a significant liturgical language in Theravada Buddhism, which is practiced primarily in Sri Lanka, Thailand, Burma, Laos, and Cambodia.
 
• Although Pali is not spoken as a native language today, it is still studied and used in religious contexts by Buddhist monks and scholars.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sanskrit**

 
 
• Sanskrit is an ancient Indo-European language of India, in which the Hindu scriptures and classical Indian epic poems are written.
 
• It is also the liturgical language of Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism.
 
• Many modern Indian languages are derived from Sanskrit.
 
 
 
• **Middle Indo-Aryan languages**
 
 
• The Middle Indo-Aryan (MIA) languages, also known as Prakrits, are a group of languages that evolved from Old Indo-Aryan languages like Sanskrit.
 
• These languages were spoken and written in the Indian subcontinent between 600 BCE and 1000 CE.
 
• Examples include Pali, Ardhamagadhi, and Maharashtri.
 
 
 
• **Pali Canon (Tipitaka)**
 
 
• The Pali Canon, also known as the Tipitaka, is the collection of primary scriptures in Theravada Buddhism.
 
• It is divided into three "baskets" (pitakas): the Vinaya Pitaka (monastic rules), the Sutta Pitaka (discourses), and the Abhidhamma Pitaka (philosophical and doctrinal analysis).
 
• These texts form the doctrinal foundation of Theravada Buddhism.
 
 
 
• **Theravada Buddhism**
 
 
• Theravada Buddhism, meaning "Teaching of the Elders," is the oldest surviving Buddhist school.
 
• It emphasizes the teachings of the Pali Canon and the practice of meditation and ethical conduct.
 
• It is the dominant form of Buddhism in Sri Lanka, Thailand, Burma, Laos, and Cambodia.
